title: Computational Analysis and In Vitro Verification Insights into Quercetin's Suppression of Neuroinflammation in BV2 Microglia through NF-kappaB Pathway Inhibition.
authors: Hsieh, Cheng-Yang; Chuang, Cheng-Hung; Gomez, Marineil C; Tayo, Lemmuel L; Huang, Shu-Ming; Tsai, Po-Wei
one_liner_zh: 该文研究槲皮素抑制小胶质细胞神经炎症的NF-κB通路，含分子对接但对象为蛋白-蛋白互作，非蛋白质-DNA互作体系，方法仅简单对接，与本课题关联弱。
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Neuroinflammation, primarily mediated by activated microglia, is a significant contributor to neurodegenerative diseases, such as Alzheimer's and Parkinson's disease. Quercetin (QCT), a dietary flavonoid, has demonstrated anti-inflammatory and neuroprotective properties; however, the detailed molecular mechanisms behind these effects remain unclear. This study aimed to investigate the anti-inflammatory actions of QCT, particularly focusing on its potential to suppress the activation of microglia and subsequent neuroinflammation. METHODS: BV2 microglial cells were stimulated with lipopolysaccharide (LPS) to induce an inflammatory response and were subsequently treated with various concentrations of QCT. Cell viability was assessed using the MTT assay. Levels of pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL-6, TNF- alpha) and nitric oxide (NO) were quantified through ELISA and Griess reaction methods, respectively. Western blot analysis was conducted to examine inducible nitric oxide synthase (i- NOS), NF-kappaB, IkappaBalpha, and phosphorylated IkappaBalpha protein expressions. In silico approaches, including protein-protein interaction (PPI) network analysis and molecular docking, were employed to explore potential molecular mechanisms involving NF-kappaB signaling pathways. RESULTS: Treatment with QCT significantly reduced the secretion of IL-6 (96%) and TNF-alpha (87%), as well as NO production (42%), in a dose-dependent manner. Western blot results demonstrated a marked reduction in iNOS expression and inhibition of NF-kappaB activation through reduced phosphorylation of IkappaBalpha following QCT treatment. Molecular docking indicated a strong binding affinity between QCT and IKKbeta, suggesting inhibition of the NF-kappaB pathway. DISCUSSION: The findings indicated QCT to exert potent anti-inflammatory effects in LPS-stimulated BV2 cells by modulating key proteins involved in the NF-kappaB signaling pathway. Specifically, the docking results implied QCT's direct interaction with the catalytic subunit IKKbeta, inhibiting IkappaBalpha phosphorylation and subsequent NF-kappaB activation. The results have been found to be consistent with previous literature, reinforcing QCT's role in reducing neuroinflammation through specific molecular targets and pathways. Further in vivo studies are necessary to validate the findings. CONCLUSION: Quercetin effectively suppressed neuroinflammation in microglial cells through inhibition of the NF-kappaB signaling pathway, reducing levels of critical pro-inflammatory mediators. The outcomes have highlighted the potential of quercetin as a preventive nutraceutical for neurodegenerative diseases, necessitating future in vivo investigations to confirm its therapeutic efficacy.
abstract_zh: 引言：神经炎症主要由活化的小胶质细胞介导，是神经退行性疾病（如阿尔茨海默病和帕金森病）的重要促成因素。槲皮素（QCT）作为一种膳食类黄酮，已显示出抗炎和神经保护特性；然而，这些效应背后的详细分子机制仍不清楚。本研究旨在探讨QCT的抗炎作用，特别关注其抑制小胶质细胞活化及后续神经炎症的潜力。方法：用脂多糖（LPS）刺激BV2小胶质细胞以诱导炎症反应，随后用不同浓度的QCT处理。通过MTT法评估细胞活力。使用ELISA和Griess反应法分别定量促炎细胞因子（IL-6、TNF-α）和一氧化氮（NO）的水平。通过Western blot分析检测诱导型一氧化氮合酶（iNOS）、NF-κB、IκBα及磷酸化IκBα的蛋白表达。采用计算机模拟方法，包括蛋白质-蛋白质相互作用（PPI）网络分析和分子对接，以探索涉及NF-κB信号通路的潜在分子机制。结果：QCT处理显著降低了IL-6（96%）和TNF-α（87%）的分泌，以及NO的产生（42%），且呈剂量依赖性。Western blot结果显示，QCT处理后iNOS表达显著减少，并通过降低IκBα磷酸化抑制NF-κB活化。分子对接表明QCT与IKKβ之间具有强结合亲和力，提示抑制NF-κB通路。讨论：研究结果表明，QCT通过调节NF-κB信号通路中的关键蛋白，在LPS刺激的BV2细胞中发挥强效抗炎作用。具体而言，对接结果暗示QCT与催化亚基IKKβ直接相互作用，抑制IκBα磷酸化及随后的NF-κB活化。结果与先前文献一致，进一步证实了QCT通过特定分子靶点和通路减少神经炎症的作用。需要进一步的体内研究来验证这些发现。结论：槲皮素通过抑制NF-κB信号通路，有效抑制小胶质细胞中的神经炎症，降低关键促炎介质的水平。这些结果突显了槲皮素作为神经退行性疾病预防性营养品的潜力，未来需进行体内研究以确认其治疗功效。
